title: The Donkey and the Fox
summary: A fox tried to trick the donkey into jumping into a pit trap. The donkey stood unmoving, chewing his thistle with serene calm until the frustrated fox fell into the pit himself....
full_text:
Mulla Nasruddin was famous throughout the province for his uncanny ability to confound pompous scholars, corrupt magistrates, and nosy neighbors with his razor-sharp eccentric wit. On this particular morning, A fox tried to trick the donkey into jumping into a pit trap. The donkey stood unmoving, chewing his thistle with serene calm until the frustrated fox fell into the pit himself..... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that honest patience outlasts the cunning traps of the crafty.
moral: Honest patience outlasts the cunning traps of the crafty.
